difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is an induction principle allowing properties of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces to be checked on affines and elementary distinguished squares with affine legs (source lines 1562-1640, label lemma-induction-principle). The solver must transfer the scheme induction principle to representable etale objects, then repair the failure of the distinguished-square hypothesis on the standard filtration by inserting a finite chain built from an affine decomposition, checking each refined pair; the chain-refinement argument is the substantive step. Allowed background: the cited filtration and refinement lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
